summary: Pennington County, SD tower begun on Summit Ridge in 1935, moved to a meadow near Moon Campground in 1940, and taken down in the 1960s; sources disagree on the year.

facts.status_note: Cut down and buried or burned in the 1960s; sources give 1960, the early 1960s, or 1965

staffing.status: secondary lookout from its 1940 move until 1965

events.note: Started on Summit Ridge; built by Ed Mason's crew of the Civilian Conservation Corps. Firelookout.com describes it as a 40-foot wooden tower.
Moved to a high meadow south of Moon Campground. Forest Lookouts says it was renamed the Moon tower.
Served as a secondary lookout from the move until 1965
Forest Lookouts says it was cut down and burned in 1960. Firelookout.com says destroyed in the early 1960s. The Former Fire Lookout Sites record gives 1965 (see resolved_conflicts).
A crew under Kenny Sallee sawed it down and buried it where it stood
Registered January 1, 2026 as FFLOS US 2111, SD 5

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites record says a crew sawed the tower down in 1965 and buried it where it stood. Forest Lookouts says it was cut down and burned in 1960. Firelookout.com says it was destroyed in the early 1960s. The story reports all three and does not choose.

resolved_conflicts.field: age of the standing Summit Ridge tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The National Historic Lookout Register says the 67.5-foot steel Summit Ridge Lookout was built in 1942. Firelookout.com dates its present tower to 1939-1940. This is a different structure from the 40-foot wooden Moon tower, so the story reports both dates and treats the standing tower only as context.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (43.94637, -104.009381) differ from the Moon row on the firelookout.org South Dakota list (43.91341, -104.00147). Not changed, because I could not check which is right. Staff names on firelookout.com (1941-1966) belong to the standing Summit Ridge tower, so they are left out. A Forest Service PDF (fs.usda.gov/media/62905) came up in search but is about Cement Ridge, so it is not used. No source read describes the meadow today or whether it can be reached. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 6 page reads.
